sentences.text: This appeal is directed against the judgment and award passed in M.V.C.No.710 of 2015 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-XII, Ballari dated 24.10.2016 praying for enhancement of compensation.
2. We refer the parties herein as per their ranking before the MACT.

3. It was the case of the petitioners before the MACT that husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioners No.2 and 3 by name, Muniswamy met with an accident on 23.11.2014 at about 8.30 p.m.
at Anchepalya on Bengaluru-Tumkur National Highway-4.
He was standing at the side of the road along with one O.Jayanna.
At that time, driver of Scorpio bearing Reg.No.KA-02/MC-7706 driven in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the said Muniswamy.
As a result of which, he had sustained grievous injuries and while undergoing treatment, he succumbed to the injuries.
It was further contended that the deceased was aged about 38 years and was working as Maison and was earning about Rs.20,000/- per month.
He was looking after the petitioners and petitioners were depending upon his earnings.
With these reasons, they prayed to award compensation of Rs.25 Lakhs.
4. Respondent Nos.2 and 3 have denied contentions of the petitioner and prayed to reject the petition.
5. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal had framed necessary issues.
The petitioners on their behalf had examined PW-1 and got marked Exs.P1 to P13.

The respondents have not lead any oral evidence and Respondent No.3 got marked Ex.R1.
6.

The Tribunal appreciating the pleadings and evidence on record, by the impugned judgment partly allowed the petition, awarding total compensation of Rs.8,40,120/- under the different heads as under:
 Sl.No.
PARTICULARS
Amount  (Rs.)
1 Loss of dependency 7,80,120-00
2 Loss of estate 10,000-00
3 Loss of love and affection 10,000-00 Smt. K Durgamma W/

3  4 Funeral expenses 20,000-00  5 Loss of consortium to the first 20,000-00  petitioner  TOTAL 8,40,120-00 7.
We have heard the arguments of the learned Advocate for the appellants and Respondent No.3-Insurer.
The learned Advocate for the appellants has contended that the Tribunal had taken income of the deceased as Rs.5,000/- per month, which is on much lower side.

It has considered 30% of the income towards future prospects, which is incorrect as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others1.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It ought to have considered at the ratio of 40% of income towards future prospects.
The amount of compensation awarded under the other heads are also very meager.
Therefore, prayed to enhance the amount of compensation.

8. The following points emerges for our determination:
(2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680 i) Whether the appellants/claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?
ii) What order?
9.

The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.5,000/- per month;
Age of the deceased at the time of the accident as 40 years and suitable multiplier applicable was '15'.
It is true that there was no acceptable evidence to show that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month as contended by the appellants.
However, the Tribunal ought to have considered the notional income considered by the Lok-Adalath in settlement of the dispute.
Accident was taken place during the year 2014.
While settling the dispute in the Lok- Adalath, notional income of the person who met with an accident during the year 2014 is considered as Rs.7,500/- per month.
The same has to be applied in the present case.
According to the petition averments, deceased was aged about 38 years.
On the basis of Ex.P7, the Tribunal has accepted age of the deceased as 40 years at the time of the accident.
The age of the deceased might be between 38 to 40 years.
In the case of Pranay Sethi (stated supra), if a person dies below the age of 40 years, having no fixed salary, then, 40% of his income has to be added towards his future prospects.
Accordingly, in this case also, 40% of the income of the deceased has to be added to his future prospects.
The deceased was married and having two children.

Therefore,
1/3rd of his income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
After deducting the same, the net income of the deceased per month was Rs.7,000/- and the suitable multiplier applicable in the present case is '15'.
Therefore, compensation to be awarded under the head 'loss of dependency' is Rs.7000X12X15= Rs.12,60,000/-.

4 10.
The deceased left behind his widow and two minor children.

In the case of Pranay Sethi (stated supra), Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram2 and N.Jayasree and Others Vs. 2018 SCC Online SC 154 Cholamandalam Ms General Insurance Company Ltd.3, it was held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that Rs.44,000/- per dependants has to be considered towards loss of consortium.

sentences.text: Petitioner No.1 lost her husband and petitioners No.2 and 3 have lost their father during their minority.
Therefore, Rs.1,32,000/- is awarded towards loss of consortium.
In view of the above said judgment, Rs.16,500/- each needs to be awarded towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.
11. For the aforesaid discussion, petitioners are entitled for the following amount of compensation for the death of Muniswamy.

Sl .No. PARTICULARS Amount  (Rs.)
 1 Loss of dependency 12,60,000-00
2 Loss
of consortium 1,32,000-00
3 Loss of estate 16,500-00  4 Funeral expenses 16,500-00  TOTAL 14,25,000-00 12.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.14,25,000/- as against Rs.8,40,120/-
awarded by the AIR 2021 SC 5218 Tribunal and petitioners are entitled for enhancement of compensation of Rs.5,84,880/-.
13. It is not in serious dispute that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Scorpio vehicle and due to the said accident, death of Muniswamy had taken place.
It is also not in disute that Respondents No.2 and 3 are Owner and Insurer of the said vehicle.

Therefore,
they are liable to pay the compensation.
14. This appeal was filed with a delay of 1393 days.

While passing orders on I.A.No.1 of 2022, the application was allowed and delay of 1393 days in filing the appeal was condoned, subject to the condition that appellants would not be entitled for interest for the delayed period, if they succeed in this appeal.
Accordingly, appellants are entitled for interest excluding period of 1393 days in filing the appeal, from the date of the petition till its realization.

15. For the aforesaid discussion, we answer the above point accordingly and pass the following:
- 10 - ORDER i) The appeal is partly allowed with costs.
ii) The impugned judgment passed in M.V.C.No. 710/2015 dated 24.10.2016 is modified.

5 iii)

The appellants are entitled for compensation of Rs.14,25,000/- (Rupees Fourtee Lakhs and Twenty Five Thousand) as against Rs.8,40,120/- awarded by the Tribunal and the appellants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.5,84,880/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Eighty Four Thousand Eight Hundred and Eight Eighty only).

iv) The appellants are entitled for interest on the enhanced amount of compensation at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization of the entire amount excluding delayed period of 1393 days.
v) The remaining portion of the impugned judgment is kept intact.
